subject: french
summary: French is in good shape overall: questions are short and clear, reading passages attached are the right ones, and the Higher Level written-production scheme (Top / Middle / Bottom bands as short bullet lists with a mark slider) is the cleanest scheme layout of the four subjects. The main faults are in three places. The Ordinary Level message/diary scheme prints the same eight lines three times and shows each task point twice with a bare slash dropped into it ('You went for a walk / this morning.'), which reads as noise. The whole-letter cloze card prints the word bank, the date, the greeting and the letter as one run-on paragraph. Attached 'printed writing task' and listening question pages show neighbouring questions (Q2 beside Q3, Q1 and Q2 of a listening section) and duplicate text the card already prints.

issues.title: OL message/diary scheme repeated three times with slash-split lines
issues.detail: For the three communication marks the same block of eight lines is printed three times ('first / second / third point you chose'). Each line shows the task point twice, the second copy with a slash showing where the scheme splits it for 3 + 2 marks: 'You bought bread in the bakery. — You bought bread / in the bakery.', 'You talked for a while with your friends. — You talked for a while /with your friends.' Nothing explains the slash, the spacing around it is inconsistent, and '1st Category - message not clear. 2nd Category - message clear.' is raw examiner shorthand. On the phone this is about two screens of duplicated text. Card 12 also has 'very poor to poor use of vocabulary of vocabulary'.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the five points once as a small table with two columns ('first part - 3 marks', 'second part - 2 marks'), then three 0-5 pickers labelled Point 1, Point 2, Point 3. Explain the two categories in a sentence.

issues.title: Whole-letter cloze printed as one run-on paragraph
issues.detail: The instruction, the word bank, the place and date, the greeting, the letter body and the sign-off are all one paragraph: '... (N.B. Cette liste n'est pas dans le bon ordre.) nous, sympas, travaille, famille, trouvé, la, mes, pas, j', chez Clonmel, le 28 mai Cher Arnaud, Merci pour ______ carte postale ...'. The last bank word runs straight into the date. Some gaps have no space after them ('______trop', '______et le'). Gaps are not numbered, while the scheme lists the ten words 'in gap order' with no numbers either, so a student has to count gaps to check an answer.
issues.suggested_fix: Lay it out as on the paper: instruction, word bank on its own line (chips), date right-aligned, greeting, paragraphs, sign-off. Number the gaps (1)-(10) and number the scheme rows to match.

issues.title: Single-gap cloze does not show clearly which gap is asked
issues.detail: The gap-5 card shows a sentence with two ordinary blanks and the target gap replaced by the marker '[5]': 'Comme tu le sais je suis ________ terminale et les profs nous donnent beaucoup ________ travail à faire [5] les soirs.' The two real-looking blanks invite the student to fill them, while the gap that is actually marked does not look like a gap. The explanation is only in the practice notes after the reveal.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the other gaps already filled or greyed, and render the target as a highlighted blank labelled 'gap 5'. State 'Fill gap 5 only' above the sentence.

issues.title: Attached page shows neighbouring questions
issues.detail: The 'Printed writing task' attachment is the full paper page. Card 2 (Q3) opens on Question 2 printed in full above it; card 6 (Q2) has Question 3 in full below it; card 5 (Q5) shows the start of Question 6; cards 3 and 12 show part (b) and the Irish-language version. The listening 'question sheet' on card 8 (Q2) opens on Q1(i) and Q1(ii) with its four options, and on card 9 (Q3) on Q1 with options and Q2. All are labelled 'SOURCE TEXT'. For writing tasks the page adds nothing the card has not already typed (except the illustration on card 5).
issues.suggested_fix: Crop the page to this question, or drop the attachment where the question is fully typed. Keep it for card 5 but cropped to the Question 5 box.

issues.title: Bullets and quotation layout lost in question text
issues.detail: Card 2's four bulleted questions from the pen-pal are run into the paragraph with wide gaps instead of a list ('...questions suivantes.    Est-ce qu'il est plus facile ... ?    En général, ...'). Card 5 runs the quotation, its source and the question together: '... de tous les jours. » runtastic.com Qu'en pensez-vous ?'. OL cards 3 and 12 keep the list but as hyphen-prefixed lines rather than real bullets.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the pen-pal questions as a bulleted list and put the quotation in a block with the source on its own line.

issues.title: MCQ scheme shows only a letter the options do not carry
issues.detail: On the listening MCQ the options are shown as radio buttons with no letters, but the scheme's only row is '(c)'. The student has to read down to the practice notes to learn that (c) means 'She cried on the podium.' Card 10 does it properly by printing the option text.
issues.suggested_fix: Letter the options (a)-(d) and print the answer as '(c) She cried on the podium.'; ideally highlight the correct option in the question after the reveal.

issues.title: Slash shorthand and general-conventions text in short-answer schemes
issues.detail: Answer rows keep the scheme's slashes with uneven spacing: 'Certain/some/the boys never wanted to obey him/ his orders', '(Il demande / exige) Qu'elle / que Madame Serben reporte ...'. Under 'Your placement' every short-answer card prints the scheme's general conventions ('where acceptable answers are listed on separate lines, each one is preceded by a stroke (-) ... preceded by an asterisk (*) and indented'), describing marks that the card does not show; on the phone it is a block of small grey text after the total. Card 10 lists examiner rules ('If more than one answer offered 0m') as tickable answers. Card 8's '3m' row is just 'Wrong gender (e.g. her workplace)'.
issues.suggested_fix: Write alternatives as 'Certain / some / the boys ...' with consistent spacing or as bracketed options, move the conventions text inside the collapsed 'Scheme rules' panel, and show examiner rules as notes rather than tick rows.

issues.title: Small inconsistencies
issues.detail: Mark entry is a slider on some writing cards (2, 6) and a grid of 16 buttons on others (5, 3, 12). The orange underline covers different parts of the question on each card (the whole question on 7, half on 1, one bullet out of five on 12). Listening audio is the whole 37-39 minute recording with no jump to the section. On the phone MCQ cards put the passage/question-sheet button below the options.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one mark control, use the underline consistently or drop it, start the audio at the section, and keep the passage button directly under the question.

good_examples.why: Clear diary task and the Communication/Language bands as short bullet lists with a slider: easy to read on a phone.
MCQ with tappable options, the right passage attached, and the scheme prints the answer text.
One-line question with a graded list of accepted French answers from 5 marks down to 2.
